boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the ten frozen records without dossiers in Grant's Operations Against Vicksburg [March-July 1863]; the existing MS009 draft is unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates. MS011's frozen siege interval (May 18–July 4) contains the separate Milliken's Bend (June 7), Goodrich's Landing (June 29–30) and Helena (July 4) engagements; campaign-wide loss figures must not be assigned to any one engagement. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Army of the Tennessee and the Jackson Garrison without counts; the live field reads zero. NPS says only about 6,000 troops were available and that Johnston could have had 11,000 by late on the 14th and 4,000 more by the next morning. Johnston says Gregg's and Walker's brigades were reported at 6,000 and that arrivals would have swelled his force to about 11,000; Greene gives the four brigades expected about 12,000. Johnston relayed prisoners' claims that the Union force at Jackson was half of Grant's army.
claims.rationale: Available, expected and opponent figures differ in scope; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Johnston and Gregg against Grant; the live heading lists only Grant, as Lieutenant General, and Johnston, as Lieutenant Colonel, against the frozen Major General and General. Greene says Gregg made but a feeble resistance while Walker made more of a fight, and judges that Johnston seemed to wish to clear himself of responsibility in advance; NPS calls the evacuation a tragedy.
claims.rationale: Judgments are attributed to Greene and NPS; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit. The heading ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Johnston says his force retreated by the Canton road at 2 p.m.; his May 14 dispatch says Gregg evacuated about noon. Greene says the Union troops entered Jackson between 3 and 4 p.m.; NPS places Johnston's order to disengage in mid-afternoon.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The evacuation clocks differ and are not synchronized.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 1,136 total (US 286; CS 850). Greene says Sherman lost less than 30 and McPherson 265, that McPherson gave the enemy loss as 845 including many prisoners, and that the Confederate reports put their losses a little under 400.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen Confederate 850 is close to McPherson's 845 and far above the Confederate reports' figure as Greene gives it.

open_questions: Gregg's June 22 Jackson report, Walker's report, Sherman's and McPherson's reports and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant, founded on the Official Records. Each report author selected from Official Records Volumes XXIV and XXII is a separate family of interested accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and letters or telegrams by others quoted inside a selected document are not separate families. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
